claim: Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space and let \(p,q\) be polyhedral norms on \(X\). Then \(p\) and \(q\) belong to the same intrinsic part of the cone \(\mathcal N(X)\cup\{0\}\) if and only if their triangular defects have the same zero set: \[\Delta_p(x,y)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\Delta_q(x,y)=0\qquad(x,y\in X).\] Equivalently, for polyhedral norms the triangle-equality relation alone determines intrinsic-part membership. In the nontrivial direction, equality of the zero sets forces constants \(a,b>0\) such that \(a\Delta_p\le\Delta_q\le b\Delta_p\) on \(X\times X\).

correctness.rationale: On a finite common polyhedral subdivision of \(X\times X\), both triangular defects are linear. On the compact normalization \(p(x)+p(y)=1\), every cell is a compact polytope. Nonnegative affine functions with the same zero set have the same zero vertices, so the ratios at finitely many positive vertices give uniform two-sided comparison on each cell. Finitely many cells and positive homogeneity give global constants \(a,b>0\). Theorem 4.6 of arXiv:2609.28922v1 then gives the claimed same-part equivalence; the reverse implication follows from the same theorem. All dimensions, quantifiers, the zero-cell case, and the pair \((0,0)\) are covered.

originality.rationale: The inspected focal manuscript makes zero-set equality necessary, exhibits a smooth counterexample to sufficiency, and requires an additional local-comparability hypothesis in its finite-dimensional converse. The new finite-piecewise-linear argument proves that this additional hypothesis is automatic for polyhedral norms. Focused searches of published mathematical records did not locate the same theorem. A closely related polyhedral-model preprint was available only at abstract/metadata level and is retained as a residual risk.
residual_risks: The full text of arXiv:2609.14035v1 could not be inspected in this run; an equivalent polyhedral intrinsic-order observation there would affect originality.
Both focal and related preprints are recent, so semantic and citation indexes may lag.
The affine zero-set lemma is elementary and may occur in general piecewise-linear literature under terminology unrelated to norm cones; no such implication-level source was located.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a natural complete criterion on the canonical finite piecewise-linear subclass singled out by nearby work on spaces of equivalent norms. It converts the focal source's quantitative local condition into the qualitative triangle-equality relation and sharply contrasts with the published smooth counterexample. This is a reusable structural lemma/classification, not a renamed definition, sampled invariant, or routine numerical extension.
